register.title: Creator withdrawal calls RazorpayX inside the open DB transaction (wallet + clearing-wallet row locks held) before any durable Payout row, and marks idempotency COMPLETED before commit
register.evidence: [vikram-pay:VIK-P0-01] WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal is public @Transactional (WalletService.java:249-250) and takes PESSIMISTIC_WRITE on the creator wallet (:263-265, WalletRepository.java:17-19). Inside it, executeOnce runs doProcessWithdrawal (its own @Transactional at :381 is inert: protected + self-invoked via lambda at :311), which calls ledgerService.post (joins the ambient tx, locks the platform clearing wallet row FOR UPDATE, WalletLedgerService.java:102-103), then razorpayXClient.initiatePayout (:398-399, real HTTP), then payoutRepository.save (:401-412). IdempotencyService.executeOnce marks the key COMPLETED in REQUIRES_NEW right after action.get() returns (IdempotencyService.java:157-159; IdempotencyReservationOps.java:144-148), i.e. BEFORE the ambient commit. RazorpayXClient builds the request with no .timeout() (RazorpayXClient.java:138-145; only connectTimeout at :86). Contrast PayoutSe || [swapnil:SWP-08] WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal is @Transactional (WalletService.java:249-250) and holds findByOwnerIdForUpdate. doProcessWithdrawal (381-410) posts the debit, calls razorpayXClient.initiatePayout, and only then saves the Payout. PayoutService, by contrast, persists a PENDING Payout before the gateway call so that PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob can reconcile it. If the process dies after RazorpayX accepts but before commit, the debit rolls back while the money has left, and no Payout row exists for the sweep to find. No test covers a gateway failure or crash after the debit (WalletServiceTest methods listed at lines 311-622).
register.reproduction: Static: follow the call chain above. Runtime repro requires MySQL + a RazorpayX sandbox that accepts the payout; not performed.
register.impact: Any commit-time failure after RazorpayX accepts the payout (such as the deterministic key-length failure in VIK-P1-01, a deadlock, or a connection drop) rolls back the ledger debit and the payout row while the bank transfer stands. There is then no payouts row for the webhook to reconcile against ('No Payout row found... acknowledged', PayoutReconciliationService.java:123-131). The key is COMPLETED, so a retry returns 409 forever, and the FE mints a fresh key on the next dialog, so the same balance can be withdrawn again. Separately, the platform clearing-wallet row lock is held for the whole unbounded RazorpayX HTTP call, which stalls every top-up credit, escrow fund/release, fee and payout platform-wide.
affected_features: All ledger movements touching the clearing wallet (availability)
register.recommended_fix: Restructure withdrawal like PayoutService: remove @Transactional from requestCreatorWithdrawal; commit a PENDING Payout row plus the ledger debit in one short transaction (through a separate bean so it is really transactional); call RazorpayX outside any transaction; then record the gateway result in a second transaction. Mark the idempotency row COMPLETED only after that commit. Extend PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob to cover withdrawal rows (milestoneId null). Add HttpRequest.timeout() to every RazorpayX/Razorpay call.
register.verification_required: Integration test on MySQL (Testcontainers) that forces a commit failure after a stubbed successful initiatePayout and asserts a durable PENDING/QUEUED payouts row and debit survive. Also a lock-hold test showing no clearing-wallet lock is held during the gateway call.
register.disagreement: vikram-pay (opus) P0; swapnil (opus) P2 INFERRED. Kept P0: the server endpoint has no server-side payouts flag (VITE_PAYOUTS_ENABLED is FE-only) and, combined with EV for the VARCHAR(64) key overflow, a commit failure AFTER a successful gateway call rolls back the debit while money has left. Mitigated in practice only while RazorpayX runs on the placeholder account.

register.title: Payout failure handling: RazorpayX 'failed' status is not a failure status, and any gateway exception is treated as a definitive failure and re-credited
register.evidence: [vikram-pay:VIK-P1-07] Webhook routes only payout.processed/reversed/rejected/cancelled (RazorpayWebhookController.java:109-110); other payout.* events fall to the no-op default (:148-152). FAILURE_STATUSES = reversed/rejected/cancelled (PayoutReconciliationService.java:63-64,95-99); 'failed' is absent. attemptGatewayPayout catches Exception, including a read hang/timeout, marks REVERSED and re-credits (:254-266). No request timeout on RazorpayX calls (RazorpayXClient.java:138-145), and retries use a new gateway key in retryFailedPayout (:422-424,453-454).
register.reproduction: Static; RazorpayX status names from recall of its API docs.
register.impact: (a) A payout RazorpayX marks 'failed' leaves the creator's debit stranded with no re-credit. (b) A sweep/retry call that times out after RazorpayX actually accepted it is marked REVERSED and re-credited; the later payout.processed webhook carries the real pout_ id, which does not match the row's 'pending:<id>' placeholder, so it is ACKed without effect and the creator is paid twice.
register.recommended_fix: Add 'failed' to FAILURE_STATUSES and route payout.failed (also payout.updated). On a gateway exception, distinguish a definitive 4xx from transport errors: for transport errors, fetch the payout by reference_id/idempotency before reversing, and never reverse on a timeout. Add HttpRequest.timeout().

register.title: POST /notifications/read, /read-all and /preferences return bare (non-ApiResponse) DTOs, silently defeating the FE's generic envelope client for those three fields

register.recommended_fix: Wrap MarkReadResponse and SetPreferenceResponse in ApiResponse.ok(...) for consistency with the rest of the controller and this codebase's general convention.

root_causes.root_cause: Escrow/milestone state is not enforced server-side: funding, refund and release trust client idempotency keys and caller discipline instead of milestone/collaboration state guards.

Money-path transaction design: self-invoked @Transactional is inert, plain save() defers INSERTs past catch blocks, external gateway calls run inside open transactions, and scoped idempotency keys exceed VARCHAR(64).
Verification blind spot: Mockito/H2 create-drop unit tests only; every full-context and MySQL test is Docker-gated and was skipped, so boot failures, ENUM/VARCHAR drift and migration issues pass CI.
Campaign activation rules are duplicated across create(), update(), PAUSED->ACTIVE and Meera confirm_launch with no entity-level guard (the F-0848 guard exists only uncommitted).

Authorization is per-service and inconsistently applied: BrandContextService trusts the JWT workspace claim, role/MFA/membership checks are missing on several writes, internal-path gate trusts raw URIs.

Deploy configuration drift: the committed compose/nginx/Docker config is not what runs live (Redis host, CSP/HSTS, prerender, _redirects, api cert, :latest ungated images, no backups/observability, secrets in tracked files).

Built-but-not-wired: backend features and FE components exist and pass tests but have no caller or UI (support tickets, KYC doc viewing, credit meter, contract cancel/amend, facets cache, placeholders shown as data).
Production defaults leave features off or unsafe: TrendPullJob, Creator Copilot jobs, CR-51 release gate, connect nudges, workspace AI hard cap, self-serve payouts all default disabled/unset.
CreatorMetric provenance (dataSource) is not filtered on "verified"/headline reads, so self-declared numbers present as Meta-verified.
The release candidate and the working tree diverge: money-core rewrites are uncommitted, the tree is edited concurrently by another session, and a stash touches the same files.
Customer-facing claims run ahead of implementation (RBI PA custody, TDS on payouts, 24h payouts, draft legal policy live, Meta review, OTP expiry copy).
Missing outbound resilience: no timeouts/circuit breakers on Meta/Shopify/Gemini/RazorpayX, unbounded default async executor, gateway exceptions treated as definitive failures.
Single-instance in-memory state behind a proxy that collapses client IPs: rate-limit windows, nonces and OAuth state are per-process and IP-keyed limits become global.
Stale or wrong comments/javadoc/defaults (repo comments lie): misleading javadoc, optional-parameter defaults such as FACEBOOK_LOGIN, wrong migration numbers.
No controller-level or job-level test convention: 46/91 controllers and several money/compliance jobs and services have no tests.
Affiliate settlement pipeline is broken end-to-end (ENUM rejects posting, wrong wallet owner id, funded from clearing wallet with no brand debit, period-agnostic sweep).
